CHALLENGE C0060 | The proposed fix in C0060 is critically insufficient. Checking string equality of `chain_hash` prevents swapped records but allows an attacker to alter `sealed_body` (the actual evidence payload) in the exported JSON while leaving the `chain_hash` string unchanged. `verify_bundle` must cryptographically recompute the entry and chain hashes from the payload to detect tampering.
CHALLENGE C0063 | `EvidenceStore` wraps a single `VerificationChain` loaded from a single experiment directory. All records in `self._records` inherently belong to this chain. Therefore, searching without an `experiment` filter in `export_bundle` cannot "leak records from other experiments" because no such records exist in the internal index.

DESCRIPTION: FIND — `verify_bundle` fails to verify the cryptographic integrity of `sealed_body` in the bundled records. An attacker can maliciously alter `record["sealed_body"]` (e.g., changing the payload, finding IDs, or artifact type) in the exported bundle JSON while leaving the `record["chain_hash"]` string untouched. The inclusion proof only validates the unverified `chain_hash` string against the Merkle root. Since `verify_bundle` does not recompute the entry and chain hashes from the payload, it will silently accept completely tampered evidence. C0060's proposed fix is insufficient because it still blindly trusts the unverified string.
FOLLOW: Downstream auditors relying on `verify_bundle` to validate an `EvidenceBundle` will be deceived by forged payloads, completely defeating the tamper-evident guarantees of the chain for exported evidence.
ANALYSE: CONFIRMED. The code extracts `record` and `proof` from the bundle and calls `verify_inclusion_proof`, which strictly evaluates the proof structure against `bundle.merkle_root` without ever inspecting `sealed_body`.
